'''Seymour:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[John Seymour (California politician)|John Seymour]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Dianne Feinstein]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in California}} The '''1992 United States Senate special election in California''' took place on November 3, 1992, at the same time as the [[1992 United States Senate election in California|regular election to the United States Senate in California]]. [[Dianne Feinstein]] defeated future California governor [[Gray Davis]] in the Democratic primary, while [[John Seymour (California politician)|John Seymour]] defeated [[William E. Dannemeyer]] in the Republican primary. In this special election to complete the unexpired term of Republican [[Pete Wilson]], who resigned to become Governor of California, incumbent Republican Senator [[John Seymour (California politician)|John Seymour]] was defeated by former San Francisco Mayor [[Dianne Feinstein]], whom Wilson defeated in the [[1990 California gubernatorial election|1990 gubernatorial election]]. Feinstein subsequently held [[Seniority in the United States Senate|seniority]] over fellow Democrat [[Barbara Boxer]], who was elected on the same day; because Feinstein was elected to complete an unexpired term, she took office on November 4, only 1 day after the election, while Boxer's term commenced with the beginning of the next session of Congress in January 1993. These elections marked the first time in history that two women simultaneously served in the Senate from the same state. Since Seymour's death in April 2026, this is the most recent U.S. Senate election in California and latest U.S. Senate election of any state in the nation where both major party Senate nominees are deceased.{{Cite web |date=2026-04-21 |title=John Seymour, former Anaheim mayor and U.S. senator, dies at age 88 |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2026/04/21/john-seymour-former-anaheim-mayor-and-u-s-senator-dies-at-age-88/ |access-date=2026-04-23 |website=Orange County Register |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Mouchard |first=Andre |date=April 22, 2026 |title=John Seymour, California's last Republican US senator, dies at 88 |url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article315503046.html |access-date=April 23, 2026 |website=The Sacramento Bee}}{{Cite news |last=Karni |first=Annie |date=2023-09-29 |title=Senator Dianne Feinstein Dies at 90 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/09/29/us/politics/dianne-feinstein-dead-senate.html |access-date=2023-09-29 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}{{Cite web |title=U.S. Senate: Senators Who Have Died in Office |url=https://www.senate.gov/senators/SenatorsDiedinOffice.htm |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=www.senate.gov}} ==Background== The seat became vacant after incumbent Republican U.S. Senator [[Pete Wilson]] won the [[1990 California gubernatorial election|1990 gubernatorial election]], defeating Democrat [[Dianne Feinstein]].
